correctness.rationale: For each residual rank, exact subset counting gives the displayed hypergeometric-order-statistic weight. Adjacent ratio simplifies to (p-1)(m-i)>i(k-p), proving unimodality and the consecutive-rank optimum. Coupling with replacement has collision probability <=k(k-1)/(2k^3), then the standard binomial central limit theorem and uniform CDF convergence give the sharp normal window mass. The explicit two-column rows have unit norm, clean full column rank, residual r_i at the chosen iterate, and direct Kaczmarz squared errors 1-r_i^2 or (1+r_i)^2. The bounded convergence argument gives the sharp mean-square limit. Executed standard-library exact-rational checker passed 152 finite configurations. Finite tests are not the infinite proof. One-step only.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 paper defines rank-selected small-sample quantile Kaczmarz and offers heuristic experiments; its proportional-size analysis does not imply a sharp finite rank-contamination envelope at small sample size or the central limit crossover. Older full-residual quantile methods and the 2025 independently accepted row algorithm use distinct selection kernels, so their existing claims do not cover this rank-selected result. Generic central order-statistic asymptotics are classical and credited; their implication for adversarial row placement and exact Kaczmarz one-step damage is the contribution. Residual risk remains for an unindexed equivalent analysis.

value.rationale: Analyzes the small-sample rank-selected update explicitly called out as an open direction in the 2023 method paper. The exact finite-population answer determines the adversarially best corrupt ranks; its sharp inverse-square-root corruption crossover proves that as few as a vanishing fraction of corrupted rows can dominate sample-median update probability. A concrete full-rank unit-row linear system turns the sampling effect into an exact increase in expected squared error, which motivates more careful rank-selection robustness safeguards. This is stronger than a routine bound or abstract probability restatement; it is not a claim of multi-step divergence.
